text:
vikram: heads up — I repro'd a p95/p99 regression on continuous batching when a request triggers a function call + structured output. looks like lots of tiny batches getting formed after stop-token detection + fn pause :confused:

sara: can you paste the profiling snapshot?

vikram: pasted below. main observations:
- burst of short batches (1-3 seqs) right after tool call returns
- kernel selection flips between small_kernel <-> wide_kernel causing warmup thrash
- KV cache evictions spike (we see re-warm on resumed sequences)

```
profile: decode_loop
  p50=18ms p95=120ms baseline -> now p95=340ms p99=720ms
  batch_size_dist: 1:46% 2:30% 4+:24% (was 8+:70% avg)
  kernel_switches/sec: 12 -> 78 (correlated with short batches)
  kv_evictions/sec: 0.6 -> 3.8
  notes: many sequences end with stop token detection then immediate tool pause -> queue drains small
```

james: hmm. looks like stop-token + function call causes the decode to yield early and the batcher flushes. that reduces token-budget utilization and micro-batches pick the opposite kernel.

len: did we change token_budget_target on this rollout? small targets + structured output could make it worse.

vikram: token_budget_target was 12 for this tenant. I prof'd lowering to 8 during the spike and saw batch_size median climb back a bit but still lots of fragmentation on fn pauses.

maria: could be KV cache pin churn — when a sequence pauses for a tool call we may move KV out of fast pool. on resume we pay for regen and sometimes force small-kernel path for short remaining length.

sara: two quick mitigation ideas:
1) add a short grace window after stop-token detection when function-calling is enabled (2-3 tokens) before declaring sequence terminal — gives a chance to coalesce resumed chunks into batches.
2) pin KV shards for paused sessions for at least X seconds (configurable) to avoid eviction + re-warm thrash.

james: + add a kernel-stability heuristic: avoid switching kernel unless expected seq-length distribution crosses threshold for N consecutive batches. kernel-hysteresis avoids flipflop.

vikram: tried a simple grace-window (2 tokens) in a canary — p95 dropped from 340ms -> 190ms and kernel_switches/sec halved. KV evictions down ~40%. very promising.

len: any downside? extra latency for truly finished calls? might delay finalization for short responses. need to keep a strict upper bound.

vikram: I added an upper bound (max 20ms) for grace window so we don't hurt tail. also tuned token_budget_target bump to 14 for tenants with frequent structured outputs.

maria: we should also track metric: "batch_fragmentation_ratio" (fraction of batches with size < 3) per route and alarm when it climbs. easy to write as a derived metric.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: patch/grace-window-2tokens -> staging (sha: a1b2c3). running perf jobs. :robot_face:

james: followups:
- add kernel-hysteresis flag (opt-in)
- KV pin TTL config exposed in console for sensitive tenants
- add derived metric for fragmentation + dashboard
- run 48h canary on a few high-fncall customers

vikram: agreed. I'll open PRs for hysteresis + TTL config and a dashboards ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sara: awesome. capture these in the changelog and call out the tradeoffs (grace window max delay).

vikram: will do. attaching short trace for one repro session: https://perf.internal/reports/2193456789/trace1

maria: nice work. once we validate we should backport to dedicated runtime too (same behavior).

vikram: yep — plan: staging -> 48h canary -> prod ramp. monitoring endpoints: batch_fragmentation_ratio, kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate, p95 decode.

james: if anyone hits a regression in canary revert to token_budget_target=12 + disable grace window.

vikram: noted. I'll post a short summary in #eng-runtime release thread after canary results.

sara: thanks!
